issues: Metadata matches Crossref (title+subtitle, 9 authors in order, 2020-01-27, pp. 33-44) and arXiv 2001.00973. Summary overgeneralizes: 'deployed AI systems are usually audited by investigators outside the deploying organization' is not in the abstract, which only says rising concern has inspired a wave of academic and journalistic literature auditing deployed systems from outside.
corrected_summary: The authors observe that rising concern about AI has produced a wave of academic and journalistic work auditing deployed systems for harm from outside the deploying organizations, while practitioners still find it hard to identify the harmful consequences of their own systems before deployment, and emergent issues can be difficult or impossible to trace back to their source afterwards. They introduce a framework for internal algorithmic auditing that supports AI system development end to end and is applied throughout the organization's development lifecycle. Each audit stage yields documents that together form an overall audit report, drawing on the organization's values or principles to assess the decisions made, with the aim of helping to close the accountability gap in developing and deploying large-scale AI systems.

corrected_summary: Introduces ToolEmu, a framework that uses a language model to emulate tool execution, so that LM agents can be tested against a diverse range of tools and scenarios without implementing the tools or setting up each test environment by hand. An LM-based automatic safety evaluator examines agent failures and quantifies the associated risks; in human evaluation, 68.8% of failures identified with ToolEmu were judged to be valid real-world agent failures. On an initial benchmark of 36 high-stakes toolkits (311 tools in total) and 144 test cases, even the safest LM agent exhibited such failures 23.9% of the time according to the evaluator.
